text:
William Karlsson has been a Golden Knight since the first season, won the Cup in 2023, and at 33 is back to playing a full role after only 14 games last year. He's on the ice 17:29 a night, the most he's had in a while, and Vegas is getting the better of play: 54% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice.

The scoreboard hasn't followed. Vegas has scored 10.8 fewer goals than its chances deserved with Karlsson out there, which explains his nine points in 23 games better than anything he's doing wrong. His own chances (6.76 expected goals for five goals) back that up. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has long shown why he still matters: he gets to the slot, 6.7 chances per 60 from the home-plate area last season, 87th percentile.

He's had five points in his last ten games, and Jesse Granger's posts this week caught him at both ends of slick passing plays in the slot. A shooting percentage of 11.1 and that on-ice luck are both likely to drift up. The Lady Byng winner of 2018 is still doing the quiet things right.
headline: William Karlsson's line is owed some goals
